clue.text: Mom' s tunic turned red

indicators.note: something turned is twisted round out of its original order, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Mother's tunic has gone red, perhaps in the wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned red' reads as a colour change; 'red' is really the definition and 'turned' the signal working on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is the long-standing political label for a Marxist, from the colour of the revolutionary flag.

clue.text: Honda running forward and in reverse

indicators.note: a word that runs the same forwards and backwards reads identically either way

parts.note: a model of car made by Honda, whose name reads the same in both directions

explanation.surface: A car being driven both forwards and backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about driving a car; the 'reverse' is about reading the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Civic is a long-running Honda car model, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Bird with a computer — how cute

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
aw is the sound people make at something sweet

explanation.surface: A pet bird sitting at a laptop, which onlookers find adorable.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large, brightly coloured parrot of Central and South America.

clue.text: Leaders of progressive trade unions split coffee container increase

indicators.note: something split is broken open, so another piece can be put into the gap

parts.note: an urn is a large vessel for serving coffee or tea

indicators.note: the leaders of a group of words are the letters at the front of each

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Left-leaning union bosses fall out over the office coffee urn and demand a rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like a verb about the unions dividing; it tells you to break open the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is a rise or improvement, the noun sense of increase.

clue.text: Crassness, as a cynic lied deviously

indicators.note: doing something deviously means taking a crooked, roundabout route, so the letters go astray

parts.note: the three words taken as written

explanation.surface: Tactless behaviour, as when a sceptic told a sly falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Indelicacy is a lack of tact or refinement, the quality of being coarse.

clue.text: See 6
Stick Bugs Bunny, say, with disgusting receptacle

parts.note: to spit is to skewer, as with meat on a rod for roasting
Bugs Bunny is an example of a cartoon character, a toon

explanation.surface: Someone is told to jab the famous rabbit and toss him into a vile bin.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is split across two lights in the grid, 6 Across and 5 Down. 'Stick' looks like a noun but works as the verb meaning to skewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spittoon is a bowl for people to spit into, an unpleasant container by any standard.

clue.text: It's characterized by extraordinary escape involving acceleration and gravity!

definitions.text: It's characterized by extraordinary escape involving acceleration and gravity!

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters leave their usual order

parts.note: taken as written
a is the physics symbol for acceleration
g is the symbol for the acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: An era marked by rockets breaking free of the Earth's pull.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the era of spaceflight is defined by rockets accelerating to escape gravity.
explanation.definitionFit: The space age is the period since the late 1950s marked by rocket launches and exploration beyond Earth.

clue.text: One dialect in translation

indicators.note: a translation carries words into another form, so the letters are recast

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: A single regional way of speaking, rendered in another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: 'One' can mean the same, as in 'they are one and the same', which is what identical says.

clue.text: Abandoned and dissolute, Dave adopts a pet

indicators.note: adopting something means taking it into the household, so one piece is taken inside another
a dissolute person has come loose from good order, so the name is loosened into a new arrangement

parts.note: the name taken as written
a cat is a typical household pet

explanation.surface: A debauched man named Dave, apparently abandoned, takes in a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned and dissolute' looks like a pair of descriptions of Dave; only the first is the definition, the second is the signal to rearrange his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that has been vacated has been left empty by those who occupied it, so it is deserted.

clue.text: Catapult is orange, shockingly

indicators.note: something done shockingly is done in a startling, disordered way, so the letters are jolted out of order

parts.note: the colour taken as written

explanation.surface: A siege engine has been painted a startling shade of orange.
explanation.walkthrough: An onager was a Roman stone-throwing siege engine, named after the wild ass for its kick.
explanation.definitionFit: The onager is a historic torsion weapon that hurled stones, which is a type of catapult.

clue.text: Yellow beef upset Daryl

parts.note: beef comes from a cow

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disturbed, so the name after it is jumbled

parts.note: the name taken as written

explanation.surface: Some spoiled, yellowing beef has made Daryl unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow beef' reads as meat gone off; 'Yellow' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is informal slang for lacking courage, the same as being a coward.

clue.text: Swivel to spoil a place for a flower (one that's in a hole)

indicators.note: to swivel is to spin round to face the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to rot is to go bad, or spoil
a flower bed is where flowers are planted

explanation.surface: A gardener twists round and ruins the patch reserved for one bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis looks like an aside about the flower; it is the definition. Being in a hole is an idiom for being in trouble, especially owing money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deep in debt is said to be in a hole financially, which describes a person who owes money.

clue.text: Note West Coast airport chill

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
LAX is the code for Los Angeles International Airport

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the Los Angeles airport feels cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chill' reads as cold weather; it is the slang verb for unwinding.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill, in informal speech, is to calm down and take it easy.

clue.text: Storyteller is perverse ogler, captivated by elite group

indicators.note: something captivated is held captive, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

indicators.note: perverse means twisted away from what is normal, so the letters are twisted

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A narrator turns out to be a creepy starer, enthralled by the celebrity crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegorist writes allegories, stories whose characters carry a hidden moral meaning.

clue.text: Rank one who binds?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a level or row in a graded series
second meaning: a person who ties things, read as tie plus the agent ending

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is a made-up word: someone who ties is a 'tie-er', which is spelt like the word for a level.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one rank in a stack of levels, and someone who ties knots could whimsically be called one.

clue.text: Singularly, 21A cooked a fish that might exhibit the colors mentioned in order in seven clues

definitions.text: a fish that might exhibit the colors mentioned in order in seven clues

indicators.note: food that is cooked is changed in form, so the letters are mixed up
singularly means in the singular, so the plural ending is dropped

parts.note: the answer to the clue about teaching trumpet players

explanation.surface: A cooked fish displaying the colours named across the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The seven colours of the rainbow, red to violet, appear in order in 1, 9, 10, 16, 22, 26 and 29 Across, pointing to the rainbow variety of this fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow trout is a freshwater fish with a pink-to-violet iridescent stripe along its side.

clue.text: Randomly relocate opening for lecturer in one kind of college

indicators.note: randomly means without any set order, so the letters are put in a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A university arbitrarily moves a teaching post to another campus.
explanation.walkthrough: The US Electoral College is the body of electors who formally choose the president.
explanation.definitionFit: Electoral is an adjective naming one kind of college, the body that elects the American president.

clue.text: Green decor stripped: something taken from a tree (one California laurel) at last

indicators.note: a word stripped has its outer layer peeled away, leaving only the inner letters

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters removed
a log is a length of wood cut from a tree
the Roman numeral for one
the US postal abbreviation for the state

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An environmentally minded decorator strips a room and brings in a cutting from a California laurel tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The California laurel is a real tree, so the parenthesis reads as one item; it is three separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is the everyday word for environmentally friendly, which is what ecological describes.

clue.text: Unusual set and star in Knocked Up — this might affect you if you were knocked up

definitions.text: this might affect you if you were knocked up

indicators.note: unusual means not in the normal form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Seth Rogen starred in the 2007 comedy Knocked Up

explanation.surface: A film set and its lead actor in a pregnancy comedy, with a nod to the subject of that film.
explanation.walkthrough: Knocked Up is a comedy about an unplanned pregnancy, and the clue reuses the phrase in its slang sense of being pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrogen is a hormone whose levels rise sharply during pregnancy, so it would affect an expectant mother.

clue.text: Everyone knows that recent pose is affected

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: It is common knowledge that some celebrity's latest posture is put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' reads as 'pretentious', describing the pose; here it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An open secret is supposedly confidential information that is in fact widely known.

clue.text: Transmission about long fiber

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a fax is a document transmitted over a phone line
L is the standard abbreviation for long

explanation.surface: A message concerning a lengthy strand of material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long fiber' looks like one phrase; 'long' is wordplay and 'fiber' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax is the plant whose stem fibres are spun into linen thread.

clue.text: Altogether, command given to a dog with respect to a basket?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: entirely, as a whole

definitions.text: command given to a dog with respect to a basket?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: telling Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz to get into her basket

explanation.walkthrough: Toto rides in Dorothy's basket in The Wizard of Oz; the question mark flags that the Latin phrase is being read as an order to him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means as a whole or completely, an adverb matching altogether.

clue.text: Teaches trumpet players to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard means the words are taken by ear rather than by spelling

parts.note: people who toot on trumpets

explanation.surface: Someone instructs trumpeters so that they can make themselves heard.
explanation.walkthrough: In American speech, where the T between vowels softens, 'tooters' and 'tutors' sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor is to give someone private instruction, so tutors is another verb form for teaches.

clue.text: Blue item that might keep a fracture warm?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sad, low in spirits

definitions.text: item that might keep a fracture warm?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: a plaster support for a broken limb padded with soft feathers

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: split the answer into two words and it becomes a feather-stuffed splint for a broken bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means being sad, and downcast describes someone dejected with lowered eyes.

clue.text: Saw commercial era

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement
an age is an era or period

explanation.surface: Someone saw an advert from another time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see; it is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional proverb, which is exactly what an adage is.

clue.text: Ultimately, post small bit of text!

definitions.text: Ultimately, post small bit of text!

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, pointing to a word's final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word
wee means small

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just one small part of it, here its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An exhortation to finally publish a short message online.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer: a short message posted on Twitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a brief message posted on the social network Twitter, now called X.

clue.text: Ain't—more correctly, "is not"—pro

definitions.note: read as 'is not pro', a phrase standing for the adjective

indicators.note: correcting something means putting it right, so the letters are put in a better order

parts.note: the word taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A grammar pedant corrects slang to proper English.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a usage note; in fact the quoted words and 'pro' run together as 'is not pro'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone anti a thing is opposed to it, the opposite of being in favour.

clue.text: Start to rig indigo cargo

indicators.note: cargo is what a vessel carries inside it, so the words before it are carrying the answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin loading a ship with indigo dye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to rig' looks like a first-letter instruction; 'Start' is the definition and 'cargo' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The origin of something is the point where it begins.

clue.text: Separate one, very dead

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
so means very, as in 'so tired'
the late So-and-so is someone who has died

explanation.surface: Someone is to be set apart, being thoroughly deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate something is to set it apart from others, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stuff langoustine guts for dessert

indicators.note: the guts of something are its insides, so the answer lies within the words before it

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A cook is told to fill a pudding with shellfish innards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' seems to be a cooking instruction or the definition; it is only the outer case holding the answer. A langoustine is a small lobster-like shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry or custard tart served as a sweet course.

clue.text: In time, dog beginning to terrify shrinking violet

parts.note: taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time
Rover is the stock name for a dog

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Given time, a dog will start to frighten a timid person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In time' reads as a phrase meaning eventually; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrinking violet is an idiom for a shy, retiring person, which is what an introvert is.
